Net charge-offs (b) of 31 bps in 3Q26 • Core deposits increased 3% sequentially; loan-to-core deposit ratio of 76% • Strong client and banker retention through the Comerica conversion Profitability: • Net interest income increased 3% sequentially • 8% adjusted PPNR (a) growth and 450 bps of positive operating leverage from 2Q26 • 20.6% adjusted ROTCE (a) and 1.41% adjusted ROA (a) Growth: • Generated 70% more commercial new quality relationships compared to 3Q25 • Consumer household growth of 7% in the Southeast and 8% in the Southwest • Gained deposit share in Texas and California, with capped deposits in Dallas, Houston and Austin each up more than 20% year-over-year, while Southeast deposit growth was more than five times the market rate Income Statement Data Net income available to common shareholders $828 $763 $608 Net interest income (U.S. GAAP) 2,271 2,215 1,520 Net interest income (FTE) (a) 2,276 2,220 1,525 Noninterest income 1,008 1,059 781 Noninterest expense 2,049 2,109 1,267 Per Share Data Earnings per share, basic $0.91 $0.84 $0.91 Earnings per share, diluted 0.90 0.83 0.91 Book value per share 34.31 35.63 29.26 Tangible book value per share (a) 22.01 23.22 21.66 Balance Sheet & Credit Quality Average portfolio loans and leases $179,244 $177,572 $123,326 Average deposits 238,344 231,506 164,754 Accumulated other comprehensive loss (4,919) (3,286) (3,276) Net charge-off ratio (b) 0.31 % 0.30 % 1.09 % Nonperforming asset ratio (c) 0.64 0.60 0.65 Financial Ratios Return on average assets 1.14 % 1.08 % 1.21 % Return on average common equity 10.2 9.5 12.6 Return on average tangible common equity (a) 16.6 15.6 17.3 CET1 capital (d) 10.02 9.93 10.57 Net interest margin (a) 3.34 3.36 3.13 Efficiency (a) 62.4 64.3 54.9 Other than the Quarterly Financial Review tables beginning on page 14, commentary is on a fully taxable-equivalent (FTE) basis unless otherwise noted. Consistent with SEC guidance in Regulation S-K that contemplates the calculation of tax-exempt income on a taxable-equivalent basis, net interest income, net interest margin, net interest rate spread, total revenue and the efficiency ratio are provided on an FTE basis. From Tim Spence, Fifth Third Chairman, CEO and President: Fifth Third's third quarter reflected the earnings power of the combined company. Even while integrating Comerica, our adjusted return on tangible common equity and efficiency ratio improved from the second quarter, and credit performance remained stable. Less than a year after we announced the Comerica acquisition, we completed the systems conversion with strong client and banker retention. Most importantly, the business is growing. The latest FDIC data show sustained deposit share gains in the Southeast and new share gains in Comerica's Michigan, Texas and California markets, and household growth continues to be led by the Southeast. We live in a more volatile world, and competition for deposits is heating up. Multiple sources of low-cost deposits and limited exposure to the borrowers most sensitive to higher rates give us flexibility regardless of the rate environment. We are building a Fifth Third that is better and not just bigger. We will continue to be guided by our operating priorities of stability, profitability and growth – in that order. reference.summary: Fifth Third Bancorp operates as the bank holding company for Fifth Third Bank, National Association that provides a range of financial products and services in the United States. It operates through three segments: Commercial Banking, Consumer and Small Business Banking, and Wealth and Asset Management. The Commercial Banking segment offers credit intermediation, cash management, and financial services; lending and depository products; and cash management, foreign exchange and international trade finance, derivatives and capital markets services, asset-based lending, real estate finance, public finance, commercial leasing, and syndicated finance for business, government, and professional customers.
